newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's to take A$24 mln charge on deal.
newsitem.headline: Foster's to take A$24 mln charge on deal.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said on Thursday it expected to take a charge of A$24 million plus costs following a settlement of a dispute between Molson Breweries and Adolph Coors Co.
The after tax charge would be reflected in 1997 financial year results, Foster's said in a statement.
Toronto-based Molson said earlier that it had settled a dispute with U.S. beermaker Coors in their battle over Molson's licensing rights to Coors' top-selling beers in Canada.

Under the agreement, Molson paid Coors C$100 million and would take a C$32.5 million after-tax charge against fiscal 1997 earnings. Molson also announced formation of a new partnership with Coors and Foster's to manage Coors brands in Canada.
Foster's president and chief executive Ted Kunkel said the outcome was positive for Foster's and would enable it to continue to be part of the success of Coors brands in Canada.
The proposed partnership would be called Coors Canada.
The ownership structure would be Foster's 24.95 percent, Molson Companies Ltd 24.95 percent and Coors 50.1 percent.
Partnership decisions were to be made by consensus.
Under a new manufacturing, distribution and sales agreement with the Coors Canada partnership, Molson Breweries would continue to brew and distribute Coors products in Canada.
Foster's said there would be no diminution to the combined profitability of Foster's Canadian investments following the changes, compared to the interim arrangement put in place in October, 1996.
The proposed partnership and the manufacturing agreement were subject to regulatory approval and the approval of all the partners of Molson Breweries before 31 December, 1997.
Kunkel said Foster's investment in Canada was a high return business and that the new arrangements when in place supported this position.

"The proposed partnership re-establishes our relationship with Coors on a strong business foundation. We are optimistic about the future growth of Coors brands in Canada and this partnership sets the way forward," Kunkel said.
The Coors brands, primarily Coors Light which is the number one light beer in Canada, presently account for about one million hectolitres of volume in Canada.
